Artist Casey Curran creates kinetic sculptures that combine mechanical systems with forms inspired by plants and natural structures. In this prototype, layers of delicate petals are connected so that a single mechanical action produces a rippling movement across the entire structure. Instead of every element moving independently, the motion travels through the sculpture like a wave. This type of movement is central to Curran’s practice. Using motors, wires, cranks and carefully engineered mechanisms, he creates artificial flowers and organisms that bloom, flutter and contract.  The machinery is artificial, but the movement feels strangely organic ,engineering becomes a way of imitating the rhythms of living systems. #art #artist #fashion #avantgarde #design

Janel Hawkins, founder of Sand Castle University, transforms compacted sand into detailed sculptures, from elaborate castles to animals and imaginative characters. Carving away small sections and smoothing each surface, she gradually turns a simple mound into shapes with surprisingly crisp edges and intricate details. The process is mesmerizing to watch, especially knowing how temporary the finished work is. Each sculpture takes patience and precision, even though the sand will eventually lose its shape. When Art Meets Technology Random International explores the fascinating connection between art, science, and human perception through installations that make technology feel almost magical. In Study for Fifteen Points, seemingly random LED movements gradually reveal the shape of a human figure, challenging the way we recognize patterns and interpret movement. The collective takes this exploration even further with Rain Room, an immersive installation covering approximately 100 square meters, where thousands of falling raindrops stop wherever visitors are detected. Using motion-tracking technology, the installation allows people to walk through a seemingly endless downpour without getting wet. By turning simple physical experiences into unexpected encounters, Random International invites us to question how we interact with the world around us and how technology can transform the way we experience reality. © random-international.com #RandomInternational #InteractiveArt #KineticArt #ArtAndTechnology #ImmersiveArt
